- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.77) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.23) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.27–0.53), model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend — adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day true values.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.27), model underestimates and fails to capture mean reversion — increase forecast by 2–5% to reflect stronger rebound potential.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window — reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% to avoid premature peak.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.80 → -0.23 → +0.80), model tends to misread momentum — apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before forecasting.
